gotcha.title: Writing the crate name with a hyphen
gotcha.looks_fine: In Go and JavaScript the name you install is the name you import, hyphens and all, so you would expect the same here.
gotcha.rust_sees: Crate names may contain hyphens, but names in Rust code can't. A hyphen means minus.
gotcha.why: So Cargo quietly turns every `-` into `_` for your code: the crate `unicode-segmentation` is `unicode_segmentation` inside Rust. You'll see this with `tokio-util` (`tokio_util`), `async-trait` (`async_trait`) and many others. A crate that is already published with an underscore, like `serde_json`, needs no change.

fixed.name: src/main.rs

go.says: Go imports use the module path exactly as written, hyphens and all.

typescript.says: An import specifier is a string, so `import x from "my-pkg"` works, and it is the same name you gave `npm install`.

python.says: `import unicode-segmentation` is a `SyntaxError` in Python (I ran it). The name you `pip install` is also often not the name you import: `python-dateutil` is imported as `dateutil`.

java.says: A hyphen is not allowed in a Java package or class name: `import a-b.C;` fails with `'.' expected` (I ran it). The Maven coordinate you add to the build is written separately from the package you import.

kotlin.says: An import can't contain a hyphen, and the build coordinate you install is written separately from the import: `kotlinx-coroutines-core` is imported as `kotlinx.coroutines`.

csharp.says: A namespace is a dotted list of identifiers, which can't contain a hyphen. The NuGet package id you install is written separately from the `using` line. (I did not run this one.)

c.says: There is no package import: a header's file name may contain hyphens, as in `#include <my-lib.h>`. (I did not run this one.)
